sources.entry: Tamari - Recipe manager web app with a built-in collection of recipes. Organize by favorites and categories, create shopping lists, and plan meals. (Demo, Source Code) GPL-3.0 Docker/Python

summary.one_liner: Tamari is a self-hostable recipe manager web app built with Python and Flask, with recipe storage, shopping lists, meal planning, and a built-in collection of imported recipes.
summary.what_it_does: Tamari is a Flask-based recipe manager that lets users create accounts with email and password and store recipes with a title, category, description, times, servings, URL, nutrition info, ingredients, instructions, and a photo. Recipes are private by default but can be made public and shared by URL. Users can mark favorites, organize by category, and search as they type. The app includes an Explore section with a collection of over 400,000 recipes from 300 recipe sharing websites, which can be imported into "My Recipes" with one click. Shopping lists can be kept per store, filled with a recipe's ingredients in one click, and checked off while shopping; the README also mentions barcode scanning to add items. A Meal Planner assigns recipes to dates up to 30 days ahead, and a REST API covers recipes, shopping lists, and meal plans.
use_cases: Store and organize personal family recipes
Generate a shopping list from a recipe
Plan weekly dinners on a calendar
Import recipes found on other websites
Share a single recipe with friends through a public link
Host a private recipe site on a home server
how_to_run: Optional: add -e MAIL_SERVER=... -e MAIL_PORT=587 -e MAIL_USE_TLS=1 -e MAIL_USERNAME=... -e MAIL_PASSWORD=... to enable password reset emails
Manual (Debian 12 / Ubuntu 24.10): install python3, python3-venv, git and the listed system libraries (libpango, libcairo2, etc.)
git clone the repo, cd Tamari, python3 -m venv venv, source venv/bin/activate, pip install -r requirements.txt
flask db init && flask db migrate -m "Initial" && flask db upgrade, then export FLASK_APP=tamari.py
gunicorn -b 0.0.0.0:4888 -w 4 app:app, then open the app in a browser
notable: Built-in collection of over 400,000 recipes from 300 recipe sharing websites, importable with one click
Shopping lists per store with one-click addition of a recipe's ingredients
Meal Planner that assigns recipes to dates up to 30 days in advance
Recipes are private by default and can be shared via a public URL
Comprehensive REST API for recipes, shopping lists, and meal plans
caveats: Manual installation requires several system packages and database migration steps; Docker is the simpler path
Password reset by email only works if mail settings are configured
The README does not describe the license beyond the metadata; documentation for usage and upgrades is hosted externally
